paragraphs: AutoRPA addresses the cost of repeatedly asking a language model to reason through similar graphical interface tasks. Agents can handle multistep interactions, but repeating their reasoning consumes tokens and time. Traditional robotic process automation offers efficient execution, while requiring substantial manual work to create and maintain its scripts.

The framework converts interaction histories into reusable automation functions through a translator and builder pipeline. The translator turns actions tied to a particular interaction into more general procedures. The builder then uses retrieval over multiple trajectories to synthesize functions that capture reusable decision logic. This makes past agent behavior a source of automation code.

AutoRPA also verifies and repairs that code through a hybrid process: it executes the automation and uses a reasoning agent as a fallback during refinement. Across multiple GUI environments, the generated functions solve similar tasks with reported token reductions of 82–96%. These findings support reusing distilled procedures for repetitive work while retaining agent assistance during repair.
icml-2026-autorpa-efficient-gui-automati.tldr: AutoRPA turns GUI-agent interaction histories into reusable automation functions, reducing reported token use by 82–96% on similar tasks.

paragraphs: Supervised fine-tuning teaches a language model from demonstrations, while reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains it using checkable outcomes. Combining these objectives can improve reasoning, but supervised updates do not always help reward optimization. BRIDGE addresses this conflict by learning which supervision contributes to the reinforcement learning objective.

Each meta-training step alternates between two updates. One updates the base model using both supervised and reinforcement learning gradients. The other updates a lightweight low-rank adapter that coordinates their interaction. Its training signal measures the reward advantage of their joint update over an update using reinforcement learning alone. This gives supervision a direct incentive to cooperate with reward improvement.

Across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, BRIDGE outperforms two-stage training, naive mixing, and representative single-stage integration methods, with over three points of average absolute improvement and more stable training. The authors also report extension to logical reasoning, transfer to code and science without additional training, and robustness under noisy rewards. These results support learning the relationship between objectives instead of relying only on a fixed mixture or schedule.
icml-2026-beyond-two-stage-training-coop.tldr: BRIDGE learns to make supervised updates cooperate with reinforcement learning, improving reasoning performance and training stability.

paragraphs: This paper studies how chain-of-thought changes what a Transformer can compute through in-context learning. Its focus is simulating gradient descent for an N-layer neural network within the context sequence. A single forward pass through a Transformer with fixed depth and hidden size has limited capacity for this computation; larger simulated models or additional optimization steps require more architectural capacity.

The proposed construction uses the growing chain-of-thought sequence as additional workspace. Intermediate computations can occupy successive parts of that sequence, enabling arbitrary numbers of gradient updates and arbitrary simulated model capacity within a constant-depth Transformer. The expansion comes through the sequence trajectory, so constant depth does not imply a fixed amount of total computation.

The paper also introduces dynamical masking, which restricts attention to tokens relevant to the current update. This avoids repeatedly processing all accumulated information. The authors prove an O(N) improvement in computational cost over the prior best in-context result they compare against, and provide numerical validation. The contribution is a theoretical mechanism showing how sequential computation and selective attention can expand in-context learning.
icml-2026-chain-of-thought-gradient-desc.tldr: A theoretical chain-of-thought construction lets constant-depth Transformers simulate larger and longer in-context gradient-descent computations using an expanding sequence.

paragraphs: Probabilistic Multi-Variable Branching, or PMVB, uses machine learning to accelerate mixed-integer optimization. Its intervention is in branching: the process of dividing the feasible region into smaller regions for the solver to investigate. The method uses data-driven hyperplanes involving multiple variables to determine these divisions.

The central design is deliberately compact, with the core branching procedure described as requiring only two lines of code. PMVB is also model-agnostic, allowing different machine learning models to supply the information used for branching. This separates the solver integration from the choice of predictive model and makes the procedure applicable across a range of learning approaches.

The authors use statistical learning theory to derive interpretable strategies for choosing hyperparameters, and propose extensions intended to improve performance further. They evaluate PMVB inside state-of-the-art mixed-integer programming solvers on both classical benchmarks and real-world instances. The reported results show improved solving efficiency. The paper therefore connects a small change in how the search space is divided with a theory-guided way to configure that change.
icml-2026-data-driven-mixed-integer-opti.tldr: PMVB accelerates mixed-integer solvers by using machine-learning-informed hyperplanes to branch on multiple variables.

paragraphs: Prompt learning adapts large vision-language models with relatively few trainable parameters. However, those prompts can still store environmental cues that predict labels in the training domain but fail elsewhere. Do-Prompt tackles this source of poor transfer by jointly limiting what prompts encode and testing whether predictions depend on environment-related prompt content.

First, the method treats prompts as stochastic latent variables and applies a variational information bottleneck. This regulates the information passing through them and reduces their tendency to memorize nuisance cues. Second, it perturbs environment-related components of the prompts and encourages predictions to remain consistent under these interventions. Together, the two mechanisms encourage reliance on semantics that remain useful across environments.

Do-Prompt integrates with existing multimodal prompt-tuning pipelines and is reported to add negligible computational overhead. Experiments cover generalization from base to novel classes, transfer across datasets, and ImageNet distribution shifts. They show consistent gains, especially where domain or texture biases are pronounced. The results support combining capacity control with targeted perturbations to improve the transferability of learned prompts.
icml-2026-do-prompt-causal-interventions.tldr: Do-Prompt improves prompt transfer by limiting information capacity and encouraging prediction consistency under environment-related prompt perturbations.

paragraphs: EMFormer targets the difficulty of extending weather forecasts further into the future. Fine-tuning for longer horizons can introduce forgetting, accumulated prediction errors, and substantial training cost. The paper addresses these issues through a coordinated pipeline covering the model architecture, fine-tuning procedure, and training objective.

The architecture extracts features at multiple scales using a single convolution during both training and inference. An accumulative-context fine-tuning procedure then strengthens temporal consistency while preserving short-term accuracy. The training objective combines several loss terms whose relative weights change sinusoidally, dynamically adjusting their influence during pretraining and fine-tuning. These components jointly support longer-context modeling with reduced computational overhead.

Experiments report substantial improvements in long-term weather forecasting and strong performance on extreme-event prediction. The model also generalizes well on the ImageNet-1K and ADE20K vision benchmarks. The findings suggest that the proposed multiscale architecture has utility beyond weather forecasting, while the complete forecasting pipeline addresses the practical need to improve distant predictions without sacrificing nearer-term ones.
icml-2026-emformer-efficient-multi-scale.tldr: EMFormer combines efficient multiscale features, accumulative-context fine-tuning, and dynamically weighted losses to improve long-term weather forecasts.

paragraphs: Eyes-on-Me studies a scalability problem in attacks against retrieval-augmented generation: poisoned documents often require expensive optimization for each new target. The paper introduces a modular design that separates a reusable attention-directing component from the document region containing target-specific content. This separation reduces the work needed to adapt an attack.

The reusable components, called Attention Attractors, direct attention toward Focus Regions. Those regions can contain content aimed at influencing retrieval or instructions aimed at influencing generation. The approach steers a small subset of attention heads that the authors empirically identify as strongly correlated with attack success. Its central finding is that attention steering can transfer across different target contents and systems.

Across 18 combinations of datasets, retrievers, and generators, average attack success rises from 21.9% to 57.8%, a 35.9-point increase. A single optimized attractor also transfers to unseen black-box retrievers and generators without retraining. These results identify reusable poisoning components as a practical security concern and provide evidence connecting attention concentration with model outputs.
icml-2026-eyes-on-me-scalable-rag-poison.tldr: Eyes-on-Me shows that reusable attention-steering components can make RAG poisoning more transferable and substantially increase attack success.

paragraphs: FACT addresses a mismatch between medical images and rigid classification boundaries. A patient can have several diseases at once, and the same visual finding may support multiple diagnoses. Treating overlapping conditions as cleanly separable can suppress shared evidence and distort the features a model learns.

The framework represents images through small, reusable units of visual evidence and aligns them with semantic representations of diseases. These disease anchors are organized according to comorbidity relationships, allowing the representation to reflect how conditions co-occur. A metric-based fuzzy membership function expresses the degree of alignment between visual evidence and disease concepts, accommodating evidence that is relevant to more than one label.

This formulation gives shared observations an explicit role in multilabel prediction instead of forcing them into exclusive disease categories. Experiments on three public clinical benchmarks show consistent improvements in diagnostic performance and predictions described as clinically plausible. The results support modeling both the multiple meanings of visual findings and relationships among diseases when learning from medical images.
icml-2026-fact-fuzzy-alignment-with-como.tldr: FACT improves multilabel medical-image diagnosis by sharing visual evidence across correlated diseases through fuzzy semantic alignment.

paragraphs: EDMolGPT changes the information used to guide structure-based molecule generation. Existing approaches often use an empty binding pocket taken from a bound complex, discarding information from the ligands and solvent that occupy it. This paper instead conditions generation on low-resolution electron density derived from that pocket-filling material.

The framework accepts both calculated density and experimental density from cryo-EM or X-ray sources. These inputs support a shared approach to computational pretraining and experimental integration. Experimental density can also reflect conformational flexibility, providing a description of the binding environment that goes beyond a rigid pocket representation.

EDMolGPT uses a decoder-only autoregressive model to generate molecules from electron-density point clouds, producing molecular structures with three-dimensional conformations. The authors report that grounding generation in these physical signals mitigates structural bias, and evaluations across 101 biological targets support the method's effectiveness. The contribution is a generation framework that makes density information from occupied binding environments directly useful for designing new molecules.
icml-2026-from-holo-pockets-to-electron-.tldr: EDMolGPT generates molecules and their 3D conformations using low-resolution electron density from binding-pocket ligands and solvent.

paragraphs: FutureOmni evaluates whether multimodal language models can predict what happens next from audio and video. Recognizing events that have already occurred does not directly test this ability. Forecasting requires connecting information across sound and images, reasoning about timing and causes, and drawing on internal knowledge.

The benchmark was built through a scalable process combining language-model assistance with human involvement. It contains 919 videos and 1,034 multiple-choice question-answer pairs across eight primary domains. Evaluations include 13 models that process multiple modalities and seven video-only models. Current systems struggle, particularly on scenarios with substantial speech; Gemini 3 Flash achieves the highest reported accuracy at 64.8%.

The authors also create a 7,000-sample instruction-tuning dataset and an Omni-Modal Future Forecasting training strategy. Evaluations on FutureOmni and standard audio-visual and video-only benchmarks show improved forecasting and generalization. The paper therefore contributes both a way to measure an underexplored capability and a training approach that improves it in the reported evaluations.
icml-2026-futureomni-evaluating-future-f.tldr: FutureOmni benchmarks prediction of future events from audio and video, revealing current weaknesses and demonstrating gains from targeted training.

paragraphs: GRACE aims to make vision-language models cheaper to deploy while preserving their capabilities. Reducing numerical precision after training can substantially damage accuracy. The framework instead combines quantization-aware training with knowledge distillation, treating low precision as a limited information budget and the teacher model as guidance about what that budget should preserve.

Three mechanisms implement this idea. Confidence-gated distillation filters unreliable teacher supervision. Relational centered kernel alignment transfers relationships among visual tokens. An adaptive controller based on Lagrangian relaxation balances fidelity to useful information against the capacity constraint. The teacher is explicitly treated as a proxy for task-relevant information.

Across benchmarks involving LLaVA and Qwen families, the reported INT4 models outperform FP16 baselines and nearly match teacher performance. Examples include 70.1 versus 66.8 on SQA for LLaVA-1.5-7B and 76.9 versus 72.6 on MMBench for Qwen2-VL-2B. Using a real INT4 kernel, the authors report threefold throughput and 54% lower memory use. These results connect accuracy gains with measured deployment efficiency.
icml-2026-gated-relational-alignment-via.tldr: GRACE combines confidence-aware teacher supervision with quantization-aware training to produce accurate INT4 vision-language models with lower deployment costs.

paragraphs: IDCD addresses clustering when each example can have several views but some views are missing. The challenge is compounded when latent representations mix shared meaning with factors specific to individual views. Completing missing views or combining representations heuristically can then propagate errors into the clustering process.

The framework encodes each view into separate semantic and view-specific latent factors. Information-theoretic objectives preserve useful information, reduce dependence between those factors, and encourage semantic agreement across views. It combines semantic latents through a mixture of Wasserstein distributions to build a global representation. A Gaussian mixture prior links that representation explicitly to the clustering objective.

A conditional diffusion model then generates missing views using both the global semantic representation and view-specific factors. This makes completion depend on the same disentangled structure used for clustering. Benchmark experiments report better clustering performance and robust missing-view generation compared with state-of-the-art methods. The approach matters because representation learning, clustering, and completion are connected through a shared account of what information is common and what belongs to each view.
icml-2026-information-theoretic-disentan.tldr: IDCD separates shared semantics from view-specific factors to improve clustering and diffusion-based completion when some views are missing.

paragraphs: IO-Adam addresses the memory cost of Adam, an optimizer used to train neural networks. Adam estimates first and second moments of gradients to adapt the learning rate for each parameter. These estimates help guide training, but storing them becomes expensive as networks grow. The paper investigates how to retain the benefits of adaptive updates while reducing the memory needed to estimate those moments.

The approach starts with how a weight matrix’s gradient is computed: it comes from multiplying the input and the gradient of the output. IO-Adam tracks these ingredients to estimate moments efficiently. This shifts the focus from compressing moment estimates through low-rank approximations, as earlier methods do, to using the quantities that produce the weight gradients. The authors also analyze how this approach resembles and differs from Adam and previous memory-efficient optimizers.

The reported experiments show memory reductions of up to 30%, with performance similar to Adam or, in some cases, better. The stated result therefore combines memory savings with preserved or improved training performance in the experiments, rather than promising the same gain in every setting. The central contribution is a way to design adaptive optimizers around gradient computation itself, offering another route to reducing their memory demands.
icml-2026-io-adam-rethinking-memory-effi.tldr: IO-Adam estimates adaptive optimizer moments from inputs and output gradients, reporting up to 30% lower memory usage with performance similar to or better than Adam.

paragraphs: This paper argues that improving a language model's knowledge requires tracking both correctness and confidence. A model can confidently give a wrong answer or express uncertainty about a correct one. Treating task performance as a complete picture of internal knowledge overlooks these mismatches and can make knowledge augmentation poorly targeted.

The proposed framework uses internal cognitive signals to divide knowledge into mastered, confused, and missing regions. These categories guide differentiated interventions, so knowledge expansion responds to the kind of gap the model exhibits. A cognitive consistency mechanism also aligns the model's subjective certainty with its objective accuracy, aiming to make its knowledge boundaries better calibrated.

Experiments report consistent improvements over strong baselines in both knowledge capability and behaviors that distinguish known information from unknown information. The contribution is therefore a joint approach to learning more and assessing that knowledge more accurately. Its central rationale is that augmentation becomes more useful when the system also learns where confidence is justified and where additional knowledge is needed.
icml-2026-know-more-know-clearer-a-meta-.tldr: A metacognitive framework targets different knowledge gaps while aligning a language model's confidence with its accuracy.

paragraphs: CPBCC addresses how to infer reliable labels from multiple annotators whose answers may be noisy or biased. A common approach gives each annotator a confusion matrix describing their labeling tendencies. Those matrices can be poorly estimated when individual annotators label few examples or classes are imbalanced, and a single matrix may inadequately represent complex behavior on difficult tasks.

The method combines two sources of structure. It learns class-specific prototype annotation patterns across all annotators, then learns how strongly each annotator follows each prototype. Sharing patterns pools information across the annotation population, while individual weights preserve differences between annotators. This balances robustness under sparse data with a richer description of labeling behavior.

Experiments cover ten real-world datasets from five domains. CPBCC raises average accuracy from 68.73% to 74.11%, with a best-case accuracy improvement reported as 26%. These findings support the value of reusable annotation patterns when separate annotator models lack sufficient data or expressiveness. The result is improved aggregation of existing judgments into inferred labels.
icml-2026-let-the-prototype-guide-you-ro.tldr: CPBCC shares class-specific annotation prototypes across annotators to improve label aggregation under sparse data and complex labeling behavior.

paragraphs: MolAlign3D aims to make three-dimensional molecular representations useful for both structural generation and meaningful editing. Its starting point, MolFLAE, provides a fixed-dimensional, E(3)-equivariant latent space that can represent molecules independently of atom count. However, optimizing that space mainly for geometric reconstruction leaves it relatively weak in molecular semantics.

The proposed method anchors these editable latent representations to embeddings from a pretrained molecular encoder. This introduces semantic information while retaining the geometric precision and manipulability of the original architecture. The resulting space is intended to connect what a molecule means in representation learning with how its three-dimensional structure can be reconstructed and changed.

Experiments show high-fidelity reconstruction and comparable performance on molecular property prediction benchmarks. The added semantic priors also improve zero-shot manipulation, including changing atom counts and interpolating between latent representations, outperforming the prior fixed-dimensional equivariant baseline. These findings suggest that semantic alignment can strengthen molecular editing while preserving a compact representation suitable for geometric generation.
icml-2026-molalign3d-enhancing-fixed-dim.tldr: MolAlign3D adds pretrained molecular semantics to an editable geometric latent space, improving zero-shot molecular manipulation.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-Experts Transformers can still forget earlier tasks even when their experts are used sparsely and evenly. This paper locates a source of interference before expert routing: multi-head attention combines signals from different heads into a single representation, leaving the router to handle mixtures of features.

The authors show that this representation contains multiple separately decodable semantic and structural factors, with different heads supporting them unevenly. Different feature combinations produce weakly aligned gradient directions, yet many combinations receive the same route. A proposed effective composition number measures this mixing within routes. Higher values are associated with larger increases in old-task loss after continual training.

Motivated by that analysis, MH-MoE routes head-level sub-representations separately, giving the routing process finer granularity and reducing composition collisions. Across multiple backbones on TRACE, it consistently improves the balance between retaining earlier capabilities and achieving accuracy compared with LoRA-MoE variants. The results suggest that how features are packaged for routing matters alongside how sparsely or evenly experts are used.
icml-2026-multi-head-attention-as-a-sour.tldr: MH-MoE reduces forgetting by routing attention-head representations separately, addressing feature collisions hidden by balanced expert usage.

paragraphs: This paper develops normalizing flows as an approach to image generation by extending TARFlow into iterative TARFlow, or iTARFlow. The motivation is that recent flow models already show promising image-modeling performance, creating an opportunity to improve their generation process while retaining their likelihood-based training formulation.

iTARFlow keeps a fully end-to-end likelihood objective during training. At sampling time, it first generates autoregressively and then applies iterative denoising inspired by diffusion methods. The distinction between these stages matters: the model borrows a refinement procedure associated with diffusion while preserving the training objective characteristic of the flow approach.

Experiments report competitive performance on ImageNet at resolutions of 64, 128, and 256 pixels. The authors also examine characteristic artifacts in the generated images, using them to identify directions that may inform future improvements. Taken together, the findings support iterative denoising as a useful addition to flow-based generation and position iTARFlow as a promising extension of this model family.
icml-2026-normalizing-flows-with-iterati.tldr: iTARFlow adds iterative denoising during image sampling while retaining end-to-end likelihood-based normalizing-flow training.

paragraphs: OneSearch unifies e-commerce search in an end-to-end generative framework. Conventional search pipelines divide computation and optimization across multiple stages, which can create conflicting objectives. The proposed system brings item representation, user behavior, and preference-aware training into a connected approach.

Its item encoding preserves hierarchical semantics and distinctive attributes while constraining query-item relevance. User representations incorporate multiple views of behavior, including explicit short-term and implicit long-term sequences. A preference-aware reward system combines multistage supervised fine-tuning with adaptive reward-weighted ranking to capture finer differences in user preferences.

Offline evaluations show superior performance, and online A/B tests report statistically significant increases of 1.67% in item click-through rate, 2.40% in the buyer metric, and 3.22% in order volume. Operational expenditure falls by 75.40%, while Model FLOPs Utilization rises from 3.26% to 27.32%. The framework has been deployed across multiple Kuaishou search scenarios serving millions of users daily. These results connect the unified architecture with both user-facing outcomes and operational efficiency.
icml-2026-onesearch-a-preliminary-explor.tldr: OneSearch unifies generative e-commerce search, reporting improved online engagement and orders alongside substantially lower operating expenditure.

paragraphs: PhyScene3D generates tabletop environments intended for direct use in physics simulators. These scenes must satisfy physical constraints while preserving meaningful object arrangements. Dense object hierarchies and irregular affordances make this difficult, and training examples themselves can contain physical violations that a generator may learn to reproduce.

The framework treats scene generation as a sequential constructive process. Its Cognitive Topological Reasoning Chain places objects conditionally on anchors, using three-dimensional axis-aligned bounding boxes to impose structural guidance. This breaks scene synthesis into ordered placement decisions rather than asking the model to resolve the entire arrangement at once.

A second component, Physics-Aware Denoising Alignment, combines a differentiable signed distance field with test-time optimization to move generated scenes toward physically feasible configurations while retaining their semantic intent. Experiments report better semantic accuracy and physical validity than state-of-the-art approaches. Scene-wise collision rate is reduced by 40% relative to the human-annotated training data. This result shows that the framework can improve physical consistency beyond the imperfect examples it learns from.
icml-2026-physcene3d-physically-consiste.tldr: PhyScene3D combines sequential object placement with physics-aware refinement to generate more semantically accurate and physically valid tabletop scenes.

paragraphs: SemBD investigates backdoors in text-to-image diffusion models that respond to meaning rather than a fixed textual trigger. Existing attacks often rely on specific strings and a single target entity, giving defenses recurring input or attention patterns to detect. Semantic triggers expand activation to differently worded prompts that express equivalent content.

The method introduces these triggers through distillation-based edits to key and value projection matrices in cross-attention layers. It also uses semantic regularization to reduce unintended activation when the triggering meaning is incomplete. Targets containing multiple entities further reduce the highly consistent cross-attention patterns associated with single-entity attacks.

Experiments report a 100% attack success rate and strong robustness against state-of-the-art input-level defenses in the evaluated settings. The finding highlights a distinction between recognizing suspicious wording and detecting malicious behavior tied to a broader semantic region. It also shows why attacks that vary both their wording and attention patterns can challenge defenses designed around fixed, repeatable signatures.
icml-2026-semantic-level-backdoor-attack.tldr: SemBD creates meaning-based backdoors that activate across differently worded prompts and resist evaluated input-level defenses.

paragraphs: Split Group Knockoffs addresses variable selection when the relevant structure appears in groups after a linear transformation of model parameters. This setting arises in multiple-comparison problems motivated by language-model analysis. The statistical challenge is to identify meaningful groups while controlling how many selected groups are false discoveries.

The framework extends Split Knockoffs to grouped transformed variables. The authors establish theoretical guarantees for group-level false discovery rate control and support recovery consistency, addressing complications introduced by applying group penalties in transformed spaces. These results provide a formal basis for selecting structured groups in the setting studied.

An application to language-model behavior auditing finds that disagreement between models varies across subjects. It is concentrated in domains with greater semantic and reasoning complexity, where the method distinguishes genuine behavioral deviations from surface-level performance variation. The contribution connects a general structured-selection framework with an auditing task in which many apparent differences must be assessed together, making false discovery control central to interpreting the findings.
icml-2026-split-group-knockoffs-controll.tldr: Split Group Knockoffs provides theoretical false-discovery control for selecting transformed variable groups and applies it to language-model behavior auditing.

paragraphs: Generative recommendation produces item identifiers as a sequence, using available signals to guide what should be recommended. Multimodal approaches provide richer evidence, but aligning modalities does not fully capture properties that emerge only when information from several modalities is considered together. SynGR focuses on this joint information.

The framework explicitly encourages the generator to use dependencies across modalities and constrains excessive reliance on a dominant modality. Its objective is to capture item semantics that are absent from any single modality alone. These emergent properties can reflect intrinsic item meaning and help explain user preferences beyond surface-level feature matches.

Experiments on three benchmark datasets report superior recommendation performance. The significance is that multimodal recommendation can benefit from learning how signals interact, alongside information that is shared across modalities or unique to one of them. SynGR makes those interactions an explicit part of generation, and the reported results support their usefulness for selecting items that match user preferences.
icml-2026-syngr-unleashing-the-potential.tldr: SynGR improves generative recommendation by encouraging information that emerges jointly across modalities and limiting dependence on a dominant modality.

paragraphs: Flow-TTRL applies reinforcement learning during image generation to improve alignment with human preferences. Conventional reinforcement-learning alignment for flow-matching models can require substantial computation. This framework instead treats intermediate latent representations as an implicit policy and explores candidate trajectories through stochastic differential equation rollouts within the learned vector field.

The optimization has two stages with different roles. Proximal Reward Difference Prediction uses pairwise reward regression to maintain structural stability when noise is high. Group Relative Policy Optimization then improves fine aesthetic detail by comparing the relative advantages of sampled candidates. This adapts the generation process on the fly without additional model fine-tuning.

Reported results show improvements in aesthetics, text-image alignment, and human preference across multiple backbones. GenEval accuracy rises from 63% to 87% for SD 3.5-Medium and from 66% to 83% for Flux.1 Dev. Average gains across T2I-CompBench metrics are 15–20%, with performance comparable to state-of-the-art reinforcement-learning fine-tuning methods. The findings show that preference-guided optimization at generation time can deliver substantial benefits.
icml-2026-test-time-reinforcement-learni.tldr: Flow-TTRL improves flow-matching image generation through reinforcement learning on intermediate latents at test time, without additional fine-tuning.

paragraphs: This paper examines why some difficult examples remain resistant to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. Among examples a language model initially struggles with, the authors find a substantial subset that remains unlearned even when correct generated solutions are available. Having successful rollouts therefore does not by itself resolve the learning problem in the studied setting.

The authors test existing optimization and sampling techniques and find that they fail to remove this phenomenon. They then compare gradients across examples. Resistant examples have low gradient similarity with other examples and reasoning patterns that do not generalize, which the paper identifies as evidence of a representation problem.

Data augmentation also fails to improve the relevant gradient similarity, suggesting that these representation flaws are difficult to repair through the reinforcement-learning approaches examined. The contribution is a systematic characterization of unlearnable data in RLVR training. It explains why access to correct outcomes can coexist with persistent failure, and points to limitations in current reasoning-training methods that go beyond simply obtaining more successful samples.
icml-2026-the-unlearnability-phenomenon-.tldr: Some hard examples remain unlearned under studied RLVR methods despite correct rollouts, with gradient analysis pointing to persistent representation problems.
